## Data preparation

```{r}
#| label: prepare-data
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)

numeric_train <- read_csv("data-train.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(C_moment_2 = R_moment_2 - R_moment_1^2,
         sd_R = sqrt(C_moment_2), Fr_invlogit = plogis(Fr))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(numeric_train$sd_R)), all(numeric_train$sd_R > 0),
          all(numeric_train$St > 0), all(is.finite(numeric_train$Fr_invlogit)))
train <- numeric_train |> mutate(Re = factor(Re), Fr = factor(Fr))
```

The training data contain `r nrow(numeric_train)` observations, three Re levels
and three Fr levels. The combination Re = 398, Fr = 0.3 is absent.

## Candidate models and validation

```{r}
#| label: categorical-log-search
#| include: false
log_formulas <- list(
  no_logs = sd_R ~ St + Re + Fr,
  log_SD = log(sd_R) ~ St + Re + Fr,
  log_St = sd_R ~ log(St) + Re + Fr,
  log_both = log(sd_R) ~ log(St) + Re + Fr
)

evaluate_sd <- function(formula, data) {
  log_response <- grepl("log", deparse(formula[[2]]), fixed = TRUE)
  predictions <- numeric(nrow(data))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    fit <- lm(formula, data = data[-i, ])
    pred <- predict(fit, newdata = data[i, , drop = FALSE],
                    rankdeficient = "NA")
    if (log_response) {
      correction <- mean(exp(residuals(fit)))
      pred <- exp(pred) * correction
    }
    predictions[i] <- pred
  }
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(predictions)))
  list(
    fit = lm(formula, data = data),
    predictions = predictions,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((data$sd_R - predictions)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(data$sd_R - predictions)),
    negative_predictions = sum(predictions < 0)
  )
}

log_evaluations <- lapply(log_formulas, evaluate_sd, data = train)
log_comparison <- imap_dfr(log_evaluations, function(result, name) {
  tibble(model = name, RMSE = result$RMSE, MAE = result$MAE,
         negative_predictions = result$negative_predictions)
}) |>
  arrange(RMSE)

best_log_name <- log_comparison$model[1]
best_additive <- log_evaluations[[best_log_name]]$fit
```

```{r}
#| label: categorical-interaction-search
#| include: false
# Build the interaction formulas using the selected log combination.
y_term <- if (best_log_name %in% c("log_SD", "log_both")) "log(sd_R)" else "sd_R"
x_term <- if (best_log_name %in% c("log_St", "log_both")) "log(St)" else "St"
interaction_rhs <- c(
  additive = paste(x_term, "+ Re + Fr"),
  Re_Fr = paste(x_term, "+ Re * Fr"),
  St_Re = paste(x_term, "* Re + Fr"),
  St_Fr = paste(x_term, "* Fr + Re"),
  pairwise = paste0("(", x_term, " + Re + Fr)^2"),
  threeway = paste(x_term, "* Re * Fr")
)
interaction_formulas <- lapply(interaction_rhs, function(rhs) {
  as.formula(paste(y_term, "~", rhs))
})
interaction_evaluations <- lapply(interaction_formulas, evaluate_sd, data = train)
interaction_comparison <- imap_dfr(interaction_evaluations, function(result, name) {
  tibble(model = name, RMSE = result$RMSE, MAE = result$MAE,
         parameters = result$fit$rank,
         AIC = AIC(result$fit), BIC = BIC(result$fit),
         negative_predictions = result$negative_predictions)
}) |>
  arrange(RMSE)

best_interaction_name <- interaction_comparison$model[1]
final_sd <- interaction_evaluations[[best_interaction_name]]$fit
final_sd_predictions <- interaction_evaluations[[best_interaction_name]]$predictions
```

```{r}
#| label: model-functions
#| include: false
bc_transform <- function(y, lambda) {
  if (abs(lambda) < 1e-6) log(y) else expm1(lambda * log(y)) / lambda
}

sd_design <- function(data, rich = FALSE) {
  # Scaling Re by 100 changes units, not the available polynomial relationships.
  x <- cbind(log_St = log(data$St), Re_100 = data$Re / 100,
             Fr_invlogit = data$Fr_invlogit)
  if (rich) x <- cbind(x, log_St_sq = x[, 1]^2, Re_sq = x[, 2]^2,
                       Fr_sq = x[, 3]^2, St_Re = x[, 1]*x[, 2],
                       St_Fr = x[, 1]*x[, 3], Re_Fr = x[, 2]*x[, 3])
  else x <- cbind(x, Re_Fr = x[, 2]*x[, 3])
  x
}

estimate_bc_lambda <- function(y, x) {
  # Profile Gaussian log-likelihood, including the Box-Cox Jacobian.
  q <- qr(cbind(Intercept = 1, x))
  objective <- function(lambda) {
    rss <- sum(qr.resid(q, bc_transform(y, lambda))^2)
    length(y)/2 * log(rss/length(y)) - (lambda - 1)*sum(log(y))
  }
  optimize(objective, interval = c(-2, 2), tol = 1e-4)$minimum
}

# Tune the penalty relative to the training sample's maximum lambda.
penalty_ratios <- 10^seq(0, -4, length.out = 25)

fit_sd_pipeline <- function(data, method) {
  rich <- method %in% c("Log + LASSO", "Box-Cox + LASSO", "Rich log linear", "Rich Box-Cox linear")
  penalized <- method %in% c("Log + LASSO", "Box-Cox + LASSO")
  x <- sd_design(data, rich)
  lambda_bc <- if (grepl("Box-Cox", method, fixed = TRUE))
    estimate_bc_lambda(data$sd_R, x) else 0
  z <- bc_transform(data$sd_R, lambda_bc)
  if (penalized) {
    # Preserve main effects; penalize squares and pairwise interactions.
    penalties <- c(0, 0, 0, rep(1, ncol(x) - 3))
    initial <- glmnet(x, z, alpha = 1, penalty.factor = penalties,
                      standardize = TRUE)
    lambdas <- max(initial$lambda) * penalty_ratios
    fit <- glmnet(x, z, alpha = 1, lambda = lambdas,
                  penalty.factor = penalties, standardize = TRUE)
    fitted_z <- as.matrix(predict(fit, newx = x, s = lambdas))
  } else {
    fit <- lm.fit(cbind(Intercept = 1, x), z)
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(fit$coefficients)))
    fitted_z <- matrix(cbind(1, x) %*% fit$coefficients, ncol = 1)
    lambdas <- NA_real_
  }
  list(fit = fit, lambda_bc = lambda_bc, lambdas = lambdas,
       residuals = z - fitted_z, rich = rich, penalized = penalized)
}

predict_sd_pipeline <- function(object, newdata) {
  x <- sd_design(newdata, object$rich)
  eta <- if (object$penalized)
    as.matrix(predict(object$fit, newx = x, s = object$lambdas)) else
    matrix(cbind(1, x) %*% object$fit$coefficients, ncol = 1)
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(eta), ncol(eta))
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(eta))) {
    # Generalized empirical smearing: average inverse-transformed residual shifts.
    shifted <- outer(eta[, j], object$residuals[, j], "+")
    lambda <- object$lambda_bc
    if (abs(lambda) < 1e-6) out[, j] <- rowMeans(exp(shifted)) else {
      base <- 1 + lambda * shifted
      valid <- rowSums(base <= 0) == 0
      if (any(valid)) out[valid, j] <- rowMeans(
        exp(log(base[valid, , drop = FALSE])/lambda))
    }
  }
  out[!is.finite(out)] <- NA_real_
  out
}

choose_penalty <- function(data, method, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(data)))
  inner_predictions <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(data), length(penalty_ratios))
  for (fold in 1:5) {
    assessment <- which(folds == fold)
    fit <- fit_sd_pipeline(data[-assessment, ], method)
    inner_predictions[assessment, ] <- predict_sd_pipeline(fit, data[assessment, ])
  }
  errors <- sqrt(colMeans((data$sd_R - inner_predictions)^2))
  errors[!is.finite(errors)] <- Inf
  if (all(is.infinite(errors))) return(NA_integer_)
  which.min(errors)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-candidates
#| include: false
pipeline_methods <- c("Continuous log baseline", "Box-Cox linear",
                      "Rich log linear", "Rich Box-Cox linear", "Log + LASSO", "Box-Cox + LASSO")
pipeline_predictions <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(numeric_train), length(pipeline_methods),
                                dimnames = list(NULL, pipeline_methods))
pipeline_choices <- list()
for (method in pipeline_methods) {
  message("Evaluating: ", method)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(numeric_train))) {
    analysis_data <- numeric_train[-i, ]
    fit <- fit_sd_pipeline(analysis_data, method)
    choice <- if (fit$penalized) choose_penalty(analysis_data, method, 2026 + i) else 1L
    pred <- if (is.na(choice)) NA_real_ else
      predict_sd_pipeline(fit, numeric_train[i, , drop = FALSE])[1, choice]
    pipeline_predictions[i, method] <- pred
    pipeline_choices[[length(pipeline_choices) + 1]] <- tibble(
      model = method, omitted_row = i, BoxCox_lambda = fit$lambda_bc,
      penalty_ratio = if (fit$penalized && !is.na(choice)) penalty_ratios[choice] else NA_real_
    )
  }
}
pipeline_choices <- bind_rows(pipeline_choices)
pipeline_comparison <- map_dfr(pipeline_methods, function(method) {
  p <- pipeline_predictions[, method]
  valid <- all(is.finite(p))
  tibble(model = method,
         RMSE = if (valid) sqrt(mean((numeric_train$sd_R - p)^2)) else NA_real_,
         MAE = if (valid) mean(abs(numeric_train$sd_R - p)) else NA_real_,
         invalid_predictions = sum(!is.finite(p)),
         negative_predictions = sum(p < 0, na.rm = TRUE))
}) |>
  arrange(RMSE)

# The original categorical benchmark remains a reference, not a continuous surrogate.
pipeline_with_benchmark <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "Categorical benchmark", RMSE = benchmark_result$RMSE,
         MAE = benchmark_result$MAE, invalid_predictions = 0L,
         negative_predictions = benchmark_result$negative_predictions),
  pipeline_comparison
) |>
  arrange(RMSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: refit-selected-model
#| include: false
best_pipeline_name <- pipeline_comparison |>
  filter(is.finite(RMSE), invalid_predictions == 0, negative_predictions == 0) |>
  slice_min(RMSE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(model)
final_sd_pipeline <- fit_sd_pipeline(numeric_train, best_pipeline_name)
final_penalty_choice <- if (final_sd_pipeline$penalized)
  choose_penalty(numeric_train, best_pipeline_name, 325) else 1L

if (final_sd_pipeline$penalized) {
  selected_coefficients <- as.matrix(coef(final_sd_pipeline$fit,
    s = final_sd_pipeline$lambdas[final_penalty_choice]))
  selected_coefficients <- tibble(term = rownames(selected_coefficients),
                                   estimate = selected_coefficients[, 1])
} else {
  selected_coefficients <- tibble(term = names(final_sd_pipeline$fit$coefficients),
                                   estimate = final_sd_pipeline$fit$coefficients)
}
```

## Compare predictive performance

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-comparison
model_labels <- c(
  "Categorical benchmark" = "Categorical log model: Re-Fr interaction",
  "Continuous log baseline" = "Continuous log model: Re-Fr interaction",
  "Box-Cox linear" = "Continuous Box-Cox: Re-Fr interaction",
  "Rich log linear" = "Second-order log model",
  "Rich Box-Cox linear" = "Second-order Box-Cox model",
  "Log + LASSO" = "Second-order log + LASSO",
  "Box-Cox + LASSO" = "Second-order Box-Cox + LASSO")
pipeline_with_benchmark |>
  transmute(Model = unname(model_labels[model]), RMSE, MAE) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "LOOCV prediction errors on the original SD scale (lower is better).")
stopifnot(all(pipeline_comparison$invalid_predictions == 0),
          all(pipeline_comparison$negative_predictions == 0))
```

The lowest observed LOOCV RMSE is from the **`r unname(model_labels[best_pipeline_name])`**
(RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", min(pipeline_comparison$RMSE))`,
MAE `r sprintf("%.2f", pipeline_comparison$MAE[match(best_pipeline_name, pipeline_comparison$model)])`).
Box–Cox alone does not improve the simple continuous model. Adding curvature
and interactions together with Box–Cox produces the strongest candidate;
LASSO does not improve on the corresponding unpenalized second-order models.
All continuous candidates produced finite, positive LOOCV predictions.

## Selected model and interpretation

For $x=\log(St)$, $r=Re/100$ and $g=\operatorname{plogis}(Fr)$, the selected model is

$$
\frac{\mathrm{SD}^{\lambda}-1}{\lambda}
=\beta_0+\beta_1x+\beta_2r+\beta_3g
+\beta_4x^2+\beta_5r^2+\beta_6g^2
+\beta_7xr+\beta_8xg+\beta_9rg+\varepsilon.
$$

This is a second-order polynomial regression with a Box–Cox-transformed response.
The full-data estimate is $\hat\lambda=$ `r sprintf("%.3f", final_sd_pipeline$lambda_bc)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-selected-coefficients
selected_coefficients |>
  mutate(term = recode(term, Intercept = "Intercept", log_St = "x", Re_100 = "r",
                       Fr_invlogit = "g", log_St_sq = "x^2", Re_sq = "r^2",
                       Fr_sq = "g^2", St_Re = "x*r", St_Fr = "x*g", Re_Fr = "r*g")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Term", "Estimate"),
               caption = "Selected model coefficients, fitted to all training observations.")
```

With squares and interactions, an input's effect depends on its value and the
other inputs. Coefficients are on the Box–Cox scale; they are not direct
percentage changes in SD. The curves below show the combined fitted effects
on the original scale, using the same residual-based back-transformation as
the predictions. They describe model-based associations. The fitted curves rise
over lower St values and flatten or turn downward toward the upper observed
range. Differences between Fr conditions also vary across Re.

```{r}
#| label: fig-selected-effects
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| fig-cap: "Full-data fitted curves and observed SD for sampled Re-Fr combinations. These are descriptive fits, not held-out predictions or uncertainty intervals."
# Restrict each curve to the observed St range for an observed Re-Fr combination.
effect_grid <- numeric_train |>
  group_by(Re, Fr, Fr_invlogit) |>
  summarise(St_min = min(St), St_max = max(St), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(St = list(exp(seq(log(St_min), log(St_max), length.out = 60)))) |>
  ungroup() |> unnest(St)
effect_grid$predicted_SD <- predict_sd_pipeline(final_sd_pipeline, effect_grid)[, final_penalty_choice]
ggplot(effect_grid, aes(St, predicted_SD, color = factor(Fr))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = numeric_train, aes(y = sd_R), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Re, labeller = label_both) + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "St (log scale)", y = "SD (log scale)", color = "Fr") + theme_minimal()
```

## Prediction performance and model diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig-loocv-predictions
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Held-out predictions for the selected candidate. The dashed line represents perfect prediction."
selected_predictions <- numeric_train |>
  mutate(predicted_SD = pipeline_predictions[, best_pipeline_name])
ggplot(selected_predictions, aes(sd_R, predicted_SD, color = factor(Fr))) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2) + coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Observed SD", y = "LOOCV predicted SD", color = "Fr") + theme_minimal()
```

The prediction plot assesses errors on observations excluded from fitting.
The following diagnostics instead examine the full-data model on the
Box–Cox response scale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-selected-diagnostics
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Selected-model diagnostics: residual structure, normal Q-Q, changing spread, and influence. Box-Cox estimation is treated as fixed for these descriptive checks."
diagnostic_data <- as.data.frame(sd_design(numeric_train, rich = TRUE))
diagnostic_data$transformed_SD <- bc_transform(numeric_train$sd_R,
                                               final_sd_pipeline$lambda_bc)
# lm supplies the standard diagnostic plots for the same unpenalized fit.
diagnostic_fit <- lm(transformed_SD ~ ., data = diagnostic_data)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(coef(diagnostic_fit)),
                          unname(final_sd_pipeline$fit$coefficients), tolerance = 1e-8)))
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 2))
plot(diagnostic_fit)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```


The second-order Box–Cox model is the leading SD surrogate candidate in this
comparison. Improvements support flexible predictor relationships and response
transformation more than shrinkage. The residual trend retains curvature, and
the Q-Q plot shows tail departures, so lower prediction error does not establish 
that all regression assumptions hold.
Influential simulations are retained as valid observations.

```{r}
# Read the 23 test input settings and apply the same input transformation
test <- read_csv("data-test.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Fr_invlogit = plogis(Fr))

# Predict SD using the fitted model and training-based back-transformation
predicted_sd <- predict_sd_pipeline(
  final_sd_pipeline, test
)[, final_penalty_choice]

# Check and save, keeping the original test-row order
stopifnot(
  length(predicted_sd) == nrow(test),
  all(is.finite(predicted_sd)),
  all(predicted_sd > 0)
)

sd_test_predictions <- test |>
  select(St, Re, Fr) |>
  mutate(predicted_sd = predicted_sd)

write_csv(sd_test_predictions, "sd_test_predictions.csv")
```


## Appendix: earlier model searches

These tables document the initial staged searches. They explain the benchmark
and simple continuous specification without repeating their diagnostics.

```{r}
#| label: appendix-searches
knitr::kable(log_comparison |> select(model, RMSE, MAE), digits = 2,
             caption = "Categorical inputs: additive log-transformation search.")
knitr::kable(interaction_comparison |> select(model, RMSE, MAE), digits = 2,
             caption = "Categorical inputs: interaction search after selecting transformations.")
knitr::kable(numeric_log_comparison |> select(model, RMSE, MAE), digits = 2,
             caption = "Continuous inputs: additive log-transformation search.")
knitr::kable(numeric_interaction_comparison |> select(model, RMSE, MAE), digits = 2,
             caption = "Continuous inputs: interaction search after selecting transformations.")
```

For Box–Cox plus LASSO, the transformation parameter is estimated from the
corresponding unpenalized design, rather than jointly with the penalty. The
full-data penalty is at the weakest end of the tested grid and retains all
predictor terms. This limits claims about an optimal penalty or variable selection.

```{r}
#| label: appendix-penalty
pipeline_choices |>
  filter(model == "Box-Cox + LASSO") |>
  summarise(outer_folds = n(),
            weakest_penalty_folds = sum(penalty_ratio == min(penalty_ratios))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Penalty-grid boundary check for Box-Cox plus LASSO.")
```
